Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

JSContactCard.description: One entry exported as a JSContact `Card` (RFC 9553). Member names inside are JSContact's own and are carried verbatim. `uid` is `urn:vtc-directory:<EntryId>`. Base fields map as their definitions' `jsContactPath` says (`displayName` → `name.full`, `nickname` → `nicknames`, `avatar` → `media` of kind `photo`, `pronouns` → `speakToAs.pronouns`, `bio` → `notes`, `links` → `links`); community fields and derived fields are exported as vendor-specific properties named by their field key. Additional members are permitted because JSContact defines them. Carried as an open object so that no JSContact member is lost in transit: a consumer MUST check that `@type` is `Card`, `version` is `1.0` and `uid` is `urn:vtc-directory:<EntryId>`, which this schema does not constrain.
JSContactCard.title: JSContactCard

schema.description: A directory administrator exports the whole member directory as JSContact cards, a page at a time. Members cannot export. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

cursor.description: An opaque continuation token from a previous response's `nextCursor`, bound to the caller and this export; a responder MUST NOT accept a cursor it did not issue.

format.description: The export format. Only JSContact (RFC 9553) in this version.

limit.description: The most items to return, at most 500; the responder chooses a default (200) and MAY return fewer.

reason.description: Why, recorded with the change and shown to anyone who must approve it.
